clean_release.attribution: Release driver records its separate runtime identity; reducer matches controller Python bytes to that exact commit and rechecks the backend. Earlier NTT negative controls remain attributed to their own controllers.

evidence_boundaries: Every listed failed or refused attempt remains preserved; positive records do not replace negative controls.

The clean integration controller predates the follow-up display-metadata identity correction and timed-failure attribution correction. Its receipts are preserved with their original metadata, not relabeled as later controller results.
Guard refusal establishes no HOL execution or axiom measurement; a missing foundation observation is never converted to zero.
Only known file-loading APIs and supported declared literal source/ELF inputs are covered. Arbitrary OCaml I/O, subprocesses, and generated in-memory evaluation are outside this bounded contract.
Computed-goal bindings retain the historical receipt status while inspection distinguishes theorem type checks from conclusion and empty-hypothesis checks.
Warm development evidence and static dependency capture do not establish an independent ISA, ABI, alignment-premise, or caller-contract audit.
The long P256 proof was not rerun for these display, scanner, and handoff changes; existing checked receipts were inspected read-only.
Raw logs, external proof statements/sources, machine coordinates, and memory images are excluded from this public summary.
